title: Gluing chart sections with prescribed quotient and base coordinates
statement: Let S be a scheme, U_i and X_i S-schemes with f_i:X_i→U_i, and R_ij a pullback of f_i along U_i×_S U_j→U_i, with projections p_ij and b_ij. Suppose θ_ij:R_ij≅R_ji interchanges the first base coordinate with the second. Let V with injections ι_i be a specified coproduct of the X_i in Sch/S, let F be an fppf sheaf, and q:h_V→F representable surjective etale. Assume q identifies p_ij followed by ι_i with θ_ij followed by p_ji and ι_j. Suppose maps x,y:T→X_i with the same quotient section and f_i-coordinate are equal on every test T. Then for every i,T, z∈F(T), and a:T→U_i, there exists x:T→X_i with q_i(x)=z and f_i x=a. The statement asserts only existence, assuming injectivity, and no kernel-pair or transition-isomorphism conclusion.

proof.text: Apply representable_etale_fppf_local_lifting to obtain v:P→T surjective etale and d:P→V lifting z. Pull back each coproduct injection along d to C_j=P×_V X_j, with e_j:C_j→X_j and l_j:C_j→P. The injections are open immersions even for arbitrary I. Each l_j is an open immersion, so w_j=v l_j is etale. Coverage of the coproduct and surjectivity of v prove joint coverage of T by the C_j, using existence of points in scheme pullbacks. The family is fppf.

Pair f_j e_j with a w_j in U_j×_S U_i. The pullback property gives r_j:C_j→R_ji. Set c_j=p_ij θ_ji r_j. The switched first base coordinate implies f_i c_j=a w_j. The quotient relation and the original lift d imply q_i(c_j)=z restricted to C_j.

On any overlap the restrictions of c_j have equal quotient section and f_i-coordinate, so the assumed injectivity makes them equal. Representables on the fppf over-site are sheaves by subcanonicity (in Mathlib this follows from fpqc subcanonicity and fppf≤fpqc). Apply the sheaf condition to h_Xi to glue the c_j into an S-morphism x:T→X_i. Separatedness of F gives q_i(x)=z and separatedness of h_Ui gives f_i x=a. This includes empty covers and tests.

lean.statement:
theorem scheme_descent_chart_section_lifting
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} (U X : I → Over S) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U i)
    (R : I → I → Over S) (p : ∀ i j, R i j ⟶ X i)
    (b : ∀ i j, R i j ⟶ U i ⨯ U j)
    (hR : ∀ i j, IsPullback (p i j) (b i j) (f i) Limits.prod.fst)
    (theta : ∀ i j, R i j ≅ R j i)
    (hleft : ∀ i j, (theta i j).hom ≫ b j i ≫ Limits.prod.fst =
      b i j ≫ Limits.prod.snd)
    (V : Over S) (ι : ∀ i, X i ⟶ V) (hV : IsColimit (Cofan.mk V ι))
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ F.obj)
    (hqet : IsEtale q) (hqsurj : IsSurjective q)
    (hrel : ∀ i j, yoneda.map (p i j ≫ ι i) ≫ q =
      yoneda.map ((theta i j).hom ≫ p j i ≫ ι j) ≫ q)
    (hinj : ∀ (i : I) (T : Over S) (x y : T ⟶ X i),
      (yoneda.map (ι i) ≫ q).app (op T) x =
        (yoneda.map (ι i) ≫ q).app (op T) y →
      x ≫ f i = y ≫ f i → x = y) :
    ∀ (i : I) (T : Over S) (z : F.obj.obj (op T)) (a : T ⟶ U i),
      ∃ x : T ⟶ X i, (yoneda.map (ι i) ≫ q).app (op T) x = z ∧ x ≫ f i = a

tool_uses.why: The existing generic local-lifting theorem supplies a scheme cover lifting a section of an arbitrary fppf sheaf. It replaces no step of the unit route and was already an approved tool of the parent.
